proposed_rules.trigger: A bottom-of-page zone starting with 'The best no-code platform for...' followed by a '| |' link row, identical across pages.
proposed_rules.decision: Model as a global site-wide footer fragment excluded from each page's per-page block inventory, same treatment as nav.
proposed_rules.rationale: Identical text/markup at the same position on every page is footer chrome, not page content. Alternatives rejected: authoring it as a per-page CTA/newsletter block (rejected because it never varies by page).

provenance.evidence: C161 rc2 'The best no-code platform for...' + '| |'

proposed_rules.trigger: A section-level container carries only a background style (image/gradient/color) and has zero child nodes/text in the visual tree.
proposed_rules.decision: Flag for Phase 2 targeted DOM extraction rather than assuming the zone is deliberately empty; likely a CTA/testimonial banner whose text fell outside the capture viewport or loaded late.
proposed_rules.rationale: A background-only container with literally no children is more likely under-rendered than intentionally blank decoration, especially between two content-bearing zones.

proposed_rules.trigger: A filter/dropdown control node's y-coordinate overlaps the start of the main listing grid it controls, indicating it was promoted out of its natural DOM position by the capture tool (e.g. an absolutely-positioned dropdown).
proposed_rules.decision: Keep the filter control as part of the listing block's UI (a filter bar above the grid) rather than as a separate section; alternative considered and rejected: treating it as an independent content section, which would misrepresent it as page content unrelated to the grid.
proposed_rules.rationale: Its content ('Industry Non-Profit Government...') and position adjacent to the grid indicate it is the grid's facet/filter control, not standalone content.

notes: Case-studies index page: nav renders cleanly; the card grid, an under-rendered gradient banner, and a promoted filter control sit between the nav and the global footer.
